requirements.requirement: Start exactly the requested number of short jobs; even-numbered jobs exit 0 and odd-numbered jobs exit 3; record every exit status in results.tsv.
requirements.summary: A six-job run and a post-restart four-job run each showed the requested number of live children and exactly one validated result per job with the required parity-based status.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supervisor running until its children finish and reap every child process.
requirements.summary: The supervisor was directly observed running with all children, exited only after waiting for them, and left no zombie processes in both pre- and post-restart functional runs.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the previous results while appending new job results.
requirements.summary: The seeded header and previous,0,0 record remained intact, while ten newly generated and validated job records were appended.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged. Python 3.12.15 was installed through Alpine's native package manager and successfully ran the repaired supervisor before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: it records healthy pre-restart services and data, restart acknowledgement and interruption, a different post-restart boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and runtime, persisted data, and a successful post-restart workload with no zombies.
limitations: The retained supervisor.py.pre-reaping-fix backup is inferred from its successful creation and the absence of any later removal command; the final lifecycle inventory did not cover /srv.
OpenRC service recovery was directly checked, but the generic lifecycle failed-service probe is unsupported on this Alpine node.
The lifecycle snapshot shows /tmp/mandatory-reboot.log remained after completion.
Requirement preserve_results cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All major mutations had clear roles: replacing supervisor.py, installing its missing Alpine-compatible runtime, generating required result records, and performing the mandatory restart. Package health and exposed listeners showed no adverse executor-caused change. Hygiene was reduced for retained artifacts: cmd-b667a607968b448b created supervisor.py.pre-reaping-fix and no later command removed it, while cmd-0c8a02a34d7942af left /tmp/mandatory-reboot.log, directly visible after execution. Both were bounded, low-risk residue; neither was shown reverted. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified.
